create.name: The World Community for Christian Meditation (WCCM)
create.bio:
The World Community for Christian Meditation is an international, ecumenical community that teaches a simple contemplative practice: sitting in silence twice a day and repeating a single prayer word. It traces its roots to the Benedictine monk John Main, whose teaching on meditation within the Christian tradition remains its starting point, and it is led today by the Benedictine Laurence Freeman from Bonnevaux, its retreat centre in western France. The community is a registered charity with an international office in London, national communities in many countries and a large network of local meditation groups.

Its YouTube channel, meditatiowccm, has run since 2010 and carries a weekly contemplative Eucharist from Bonnevaux, homilies and talks by Laurence Freeman, conversations with guests on prayer and consciousness, and recordings from seminars and retreats. On its website the community offers a free introductory mini-course on how to meditate, paid online courses on Christian meditation, mysticism and Benedictine wisdom, a meditation app, weekly readings by email and a guide for starting a local group.
